title: The Travellers and the Plane-Tree
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Two Travellers were walking along a bare and dusty road in the heat of a summer's day. Coming presently to a Plane-tree, they joyfully turned aside to shelter from the burning rays of the sun in the deep shade of its spreading branches.

As they rested, looking up into the tree, one of them remarked to his companion, "What a useless tree the Plane is! It bears no fruit and is of no service to man at all." The Plane-tree interrupted him with indignation. "You ungrateful creature!" it cried: "you come and take shelter under me from the scorching sun, and then, in the very act of enjoying the cool shade of my foliage, you abuse me and call me good for nothing!"
Many a service is met with ingratitude.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what kind of road are the two Travellers walking along?
options: A wide, paved highway
A narrow forest path
A bare and dusty road
A muddy road after rain

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why do the Travellers turn aside to the Plane-tree?
options: To shelter from the burning rays of the sun
To pick its fruit for their journey
To rest their feet after a long climb
To wait out a sudden storm

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does one Traveller say about the Plane-tree?
options: That it is the tallest tree they have ever seen
That it should be cut down to widen the road
That its shade is too thin to be worth stopping for
That it is useless, bears no fruit, and is of no service to man

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Plane-tree react to the remark?
options: It remains silent, unaffected by the words
It interrupts him with indignation
It sheds its leaves in protest
It agrees that it is not very useful

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Plane-tree call the Traveller?
options: "You foolish wanderer!"
"You lazy traveller!"
"You ungrateful creature!"
"You thoughtless stranger!"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what is the Traveller doing at the very moment he insults the tree?
options: Enjoying the cool shade of its foliage
Climbing up into its branches
Carving his name into its trunk
Walking away from it entirely

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Plane-tree find the Traveller's remark especially unfair?
options: He has never actually rested beneath the tree before
He is speaking to a different tree by mistake
He does not realize the tree can understand him
He is benefiting from its shade at the exact moment he insults it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Traveller overlook when judging the Plane-tree's usefulness?
options: The tree might bear fruit later in the season
Shade and shelter can be a valuable service, even without producing fruit
The tree was planted specifically to give shade to travellers
The road would be impassable without the tree nearby

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "indignation" mean in "interrupted him with indignation"?
options: Confusion about what was said
Sadness at being misunderstood
Anger at being treated unfairly
Amusement at a joke

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable, given its closing line?
options: A helpful act can still be met with thanklessness from the very person who benefits from it
Trees that bear no fruit provide no real value to travellers
Travellers should never rest under trees they do not recognize
Shade is less valuable than fruit in every circumstance

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the Travellers seeking relief from?
options: A sudden downpour of rain
A swarm of biting insects
The noise of a nearby crowd
The burning rays of the sun

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what were the Travellers doing as one of them made his remark?
options: Arguing about which road to take
Resting and looking up into the tree
Searching the ground for fallen fruit
Preparing to continue walking at once

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what two things does the Traveller say the Plane-tree lacks?
options: Height and strong branches
Shade and cool leaves
Fruit and service to man
Roots and a straight trunk

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Plane-tree's outburst be considered a fair response rather than an overreaction?
options: The insult comes directly from someone actively benefiting from the tree at that moment
The tree has been insulted by many travellers before this one
The Traveller threatens to cut the tree down as he speaks
The tree has no other way of communicating its feelings

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what standard is the Traveller mistakenly using to judge the tree's worth?
options: How tall and old the tree appears to be
Whether other travellers have praised the tree before
How far the tree is from the nearest town
Whether it produces something to eat, ignoring the shelter it provides

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "foliage" mean in "the cool shade of my foliage"?
options: Roots beneath the soil
Leaves and leafy branches
Fruit growing on a tree
Bark covering a trunk

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: Two Travellers argue over which tree gives the best shade
A Plane-tree refuses to shelter the Travellers from the sun
A Plane-tree scolds a Traveller for calling it useless while he enjoys its shade
A Traveller apologizes to the tree before continuing his journey
